subject: Post-call recap + trial design (shadow vs batch) and success rubric
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medisync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed trial design (shadow vs batch)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the claims-review workflow and your SLAs. Per our discussion, I summarized a proposed trial design and two evaluation tracks so we can pick the path that minimizes production risk for Medisync while giving you a clear signal on quality and cost. Attached is a short proof-of-evidence packet and an eval template.

Quick recap of scope we agreed:
- Scope: claims pre-triage and flagging for potential documentation gaps (approx 6k queries/day).
- Data: de-identified claim records + sample annotator labels (we'll use your staging dataset).
- Duration: 2 weeks shadow + optional 1 week batch offline evaluation, or 3 weeks batch-only if preferred.

Two recommended evaluation approaches (pick one):

1) Online shadow (recommended for lowest integration time)
- Run Redwood side-by-side with your production pipeline for 10 business days.
- Redwood returns model outputs to a shadow endpoint; your system records accepted/rejected candidates without impacting user flow.
- Metrics collected in real time: top-1 precision, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), and preliminary hallucination flags (model confidence heuristics).
- Minimum sample: 5k representative queries per week.
- Advantage: measures real traffic patterns, surface-level drift, and infra latency.

2) Offline batch (structured, faster signal on quality)
- You provide 10k labeled cases (held-out) and we run the model offline on the set.
- Metrics: top-1 accuracy, recall on known failure modes, hallucination/error rate (false assertions per 1k tokens), and business-weighted score (see rubric below).
- Advantage: reproducible, allows head-to-head model comparisons and easier auditing.

Proposed success rubric (combined score approach):
- Core accuracy (top-1 match to gold label): 40 points (>=85% target to pass)
- Safety/No-hallucination: 30 points (<=2 hallucinations per 1k tokens target)
- Latency SLO: 20 points (p95 <= 600ms)
- Operational fit (token cost / throughput): 10 points (within cost envelope)
- Pass threshold: 75/100 with no single category below 50% of its points.

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood: set up shadow endpoint, run instrumentation, provide dashboards and eval sheet (Marissa will own ops).
- Medisync: supply de-id sample + baseline labels, confirm legal/POE items for data transfer (Javier is your procurement lead).
- Timeline: if we start Tues 10/26: Shadow window 10/26–11/06, interim check 11/02, final report 11/09.

Attachments: Medisync_POE.pdf (POE checklist), shadow_eval_template.xlsx (rubric & metrics).

Please reply with which eval track you prefer (shadow or batch), whether the proposed timeline fits, and any data/legal blockers. Happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Ava Chen

Thanks, Ava — this is super helpful and aligns with what I briefed the claims team on. A few clarifications: 

> Proposed success rubric (combined score approach):
> - Core accuracy (top-1 match to gold label): 40 points (>=85% target to pass)
> - Safety/No-hallucination: 30 points (<=2 hallucinations per 1k tokens target)
>
We like the combined score. Can you clarify how Redwood defines a "hallucination" in the rubric? For clinical claims wording, we need an explicit definition (e.g., assertion of patient-specific facts not present in the claim). Also:

- We can do an offline batch of 12k labeled cases within a week if that helps.
- For shadow: our infra team will need a lightweight webhook schema (JSON) — can you share a stub payload?
- Timeline: 10/26 start is tight for procurement. If we need PO signed first, we can target 11/02 start.

Javier, FYI on POE and potential procurement timing.

Best,
Elena
Sr. PM, Clinical Systems | Medisync
